For trace: count lines beginning with "State ". That requires splitting lines. Could use (with-input-from-string (s input) (loop for line = (read-line s nil) while line count if (and (>= (length line) 6) (string= "State " (subseq line 0 6))))). 

Let me write it:

(lambda (input)
  (labels ((count-lines (prefix)
             (with-input-from-string (s input)
               (loop for line = (read-line s nil)
                     while line
                     count (and (>= (length line) (length prefix))
                                (string= prefix (subseq line 0 (length prefix))))))))
    (cond
      ((search "is violated." input)
       (let* ((start (+ (search "Error: Invariant " input) (length "Error: Invariant ")))
              (end (search " is violated." input :start2 start)))
         (format nil "invariant ~a~%trace ~a" (subseq input start end) (count-lines "State "))))
      ((search "No error has been found." input) "HOLDS")
      ((search "Temporal properties were violated" input) "VIOLATES (temporal)")
      (t "ERROR"))))

Order: check "is violated." first, then "Temporal properties were violated", then holds. Actually a log could contain both "is violated." and "No error..."? Unlikely; the rules define precedence: VIOLATES iff contains "is violated." or "Temporal properties were violated"; HOLDS iff contains "No error has been found." A log with both would be ambiguous; following the listed order, VIOLATES first is fine.

Note "Temporal properties were violated" doesn't give an invariant name, so return something like "invariant <unknown>"? Actually the task says the invariant name comes from "Error: Invariant <Name> is violated." If only temporal violation, there's no name. Keep it simple: return "VIOLATES".

arguments.source:
(lambda (input)
  (labels ((count-lines (prefix)
             (with-input-from-string (s input)
               (loop for line = (read-line s nil)
                     while line
                     count (and (>= (length line) (length prefix))
                                (string= prefix (subseq line 0 (length prefix))))))))
    (cond
      ((search "is violated." input)
       (let* ((marker "Error: Invariant ")
              (start (+ (search marker input) (length marker)))
              (end (search " is violated." input :start2 start)))
         (format nil "invariant ~a~%trace ~a" (subseq input start end) (count-lines "State "))))
      ((search "Temporal properties were violated" input) "VIOLATES (temporal; no invariant name)")
      ((search "No error has been found." input) "HOLDS")
      (t "ERROR"))))
arguments.note: Parse a TLC log string into verdict: invariant name + trace count, HOLDS, or ERROR.
